source: Generated by tacenta-core (primitives/xeddsa.rs). The XEdDSA specification, revision 1, publishes no known-answer vectors, so these pin this implementation's own output rather than validate it against an authority; the runner also verifies each signature, which is the check against an independent implementation (ed25519-dalek's verify_strict).

vectors.comment: The pin the crate's own test carries (signing_is_a_fixed_function_of_key_and_nonce). secret is the X25519 private key; nonce is the 64 bytes of randomness Z the signer draws, served by a byte source that repeats the given bytes; the signature verifies under the X25519 public key of secret, with the Edwards sign carried in the top bit of the last byte.
Same key and message, a different nonce: the signature differs and still verifies, which is what distinguishes XEdDSA from a deterministic scheme.
A different key, a non-repeating nonce, and an empty message. The signer normalises the Edwards sign to zero, so the top bit of the last byte is clear in every signature it produces.
